    Kashi Tamil Sangamam 4.0PDF p. 49

    • Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS) 4.0 is a Government- led cultural and educational exchange that deepens the civilisational connect between Tamil Nadu and Kashi (Varanasi). The 4 th edition was held in Varanasi from 2 to 15 December 2025, and it put a special focus on Tamil language learning and youth engagement under the theme “Let Us Learn Tamil – Tamil Karkalam.” The valedictory ceremony of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 4.0 was held on December 30, 2025, graced by the Vice President of India C.P . Radhakrishnan.PDF p. 49

    About Kashi Tamil Sangamam?PDF p. 49

    • KTS is designed as a “knowledge bridge” and people-to-people platform to celebrate the long- standing movement of ideas, spirituality, learning and culture between Tamil Nadu and Kashi.PDF p. 49
    • It is aligned with the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB).PDF p. 49
    • KTS is anchored by the Ministry of Education , with IIT Madras and Banaras Hindu University (BHU) as principal knowledge partners, and participation from multiple ministries (including Railways, Culture, Tourism, Textiles, Youth Affairs & Sports) along with the Government of Uttar Pradesh.PDF p. 49
    • Kashi Tamil SangamamPDF p. 49
    • KTS 1.0 (2022): Held from November 16 – December 16, 2022; large-scale cultural immersion with curated tours and academic-cultural interactions.PDF p. 49
    • KTS 2.0 (Dec 2023): Held 17–30 Dec 2023 at Namo Ghat, Varanasi; included real-time Tamil translation of the PM’s address; exhibition sales and high public footfall were reported.PDF p. 49
    • KTS 3.0 (Feb 2025): Held 15–24 Feb 2025; thematic focus on Sage Agastya; workshops connected ancient knowledge systems with contemporary education aligned with NEP 2020 emphasis on Indian knowledge traditions.PDF p. 49

    Union Cabinet Approves 2027 CensusPDF p. 49, 50

    • India is conducting Census 2027 after the last completed Census of 2011. It will be the sixteenth Census of India and the eighth since Independence.PDF p. 49
    • The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the scheme on 12 December 2025, at an estimated cost of ₹11,718.24 crore.PDF p. 49
    • The Census is a Union subject under Entry 69 of the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. Its legal framework comprises the Census Act, 1948, and the Census Rules, 1990, as amended.PDF p. 49
    • The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India , under the Ministry of Home Affairs, conducts the Census with state governments and Union Territory administrations.PDF p. 49
    • The initial declaration under Section 3 of the Census Act was issued on 16 June 2025 . A notification dated 5 September 2026 superseded it and introduced an additional regional reference date.PDF p. 49
    • Census operations will take place across 2026 and 2027 in two phases: Houselisting and Housing Census, followed by Population Enumeration.PDF p. 49
    • Phase I records housing conditions, household amenities and assets. Its original national window was 1 April–30 September 2026, normally involving 30 days of fieldwork in each state or Union Territory.PDF p. 49
    • Subsequent notifications deferred Phase I in Manipur until a further declaration and extended houselisting in Assam’s Charaideo and Sivasagar districts until 31 October 2026.PDF p. 49
    • Phase II—Population Enumeration generally remains scheduled for February 2027, with separate schedules for specified regions.PDF p. 49
    • In the entire Union Territory of Ladakh and specified snow-bound non-synchronous areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, Population Enumeration was scheduled for 1–30 September 2026 , followed by revision on 1–5 October 2026 . Self-enumeration was scheduled for 17–31 August 2026.PDF p. 49
    • The reference date, meaning the point in time to which the population count relates, is generally 00:00 hours on 1 March 2027.PDF p. 49
    • Population Enumeration covers demography, religion, language, literacy, education, economic activity, migration and fertility . Its notified schedule contains 40 questions, including questions on disability and digital literacy.PDF p. 49
    • The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs decided on April 30, 2025 to include caste enumeration. Caste information will be collected electronically during Population Enumeration, and Question 10 concerns SC, ST and caste.PDF p. 50
    • Census 2027 will be India’s first Census conducted by digital means , using enumerator mobile applications available on Android and iOS , while continuing house-to-house visits.PDF p. 50
    • Optional online self-enumeration enables house- holds to submit information before the enumerator’s visit. For Phase I, the normal window is 15 days before fieldwork , and the generated Self- Enumeration ID helps enumerators confirm submitted details.PDF p. 50
    • About 30 lakh field functionaries are envisaged.PDF p. 50
    • Census 2021 was postponed following the COVID-19 outbreak.PDF p. 50

    News in ShortPDF p. 50

    Unlocking Growth in Tourism and Hospitality SectorPDF p. 50

    • NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the Ministry of Tourism, launched a report titled “Unlocking Growth in Tourism and Hospitality Sector” on June 30, 2026 at New Delhi.PDF p. 50
    • The report provides a roadmap to simplify regulations, improve ease of doing business, attract investments and support sustainable growth in India’s tourism and hospitality sector.PDF p. 50
    • The report is aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 and aims to strengthen tourism’s contribution to economic growth, employment generation and regional development.PDF p. 50
    • 12th International Yoga Day 2026PDF p. 50
    • The 12 th International Yoga Day was officially celebrated in Kolkata on June 21, 2026.PDF p. 50
    • Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in the main event at Red Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.PDF p. 50
    • Around 35,000 people joined the yoga session with the Prime Minister.PDF p. 50
    • The theme of International Yoga Day 2026 was “Yoga for Healthy Ageing.”PDF p. 50
    • This event created a new Guinness World Record.PDF p. 50
    • The campaign “100 Days, 100 Cities, 100 Organisations” encouraged regular yoga practice across India.PDF p. 50
    • The United Nations declared June 21 as International Yoga Day on December 11, 2014.PDF p. 50

    Ahmedabad Metro Rail Project Phase 2APDF p. 50

    • The Union Cabinet approved Phase 2A of the Ahmedabad Metro Rail Project on June 10, 2026.PDF p. 50
    • The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.PDF p. 50
    • Phase 2A will connect Koteshwar Road to the Airport corridor.PDF p. 50
    • The total length of the new metro corridor will be 6.032 km.PDF p. 50
    • The corridor will have 5 stations.PDF p. 50
    • The total project cost, including Interest During Construction, is `2,169.04 crore.PDF p. 50
    • After Phase 2A becomes operational, Ahmedabad- Gandhinagar will have 77.63 km of active metro rail network.PDF p. 50

    Yuge Yugeen Bharat National MuseumPDF p. 50

    • The first gallery of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum “Time and Timelessness,” is expected to open by end-2026.PDF p. 50
    • The museum is set to become the largest in the world, replacing the existing National Museum.PDF p. 50
    • Announced by the Prime Minister in May 2023 at the International Museum Expo, Delhi.PDF p. 50
    • Located in the North and South Blocks, Raisina Hill, under the Central Vista Redevelopment Project.PDF p. 50
    • Planned as the world’s largest museum, covering about 1.55 lakh m² (as on December, 2024) with nearly 950 rooms.PDF p. 50

    Jammu and Kashmir’s Chrysanthemum GardenPDF p. 50

    • Inaugurated on October 25, 2025 by Chief Minister of UT of Jammu and Kashmir Omar Abdullah at Nehru Memorial Botanical Garden, Srinagar.PDF p. 50
    • Spread over 100 kanals (12.5 acres) at a cost of `1.86 crore.PDF p. 50
    • It aims to extend tourist season beyond tulip bloom and promote autumn tourism.PDF p. 50

    Ministry of Mines Reclassifies Limestone as Major MineralPDF p. 50

    • Effective from October 10, 2025, all limestone reclassified as “major mineral” under MMDR Act, 1957.PDF p. 50
    • Removes previous distinction between lime stone (minor) and industrial (major) uses.PDF p. 50
    • Simplifies regulation, improves mining transparency, and enables freer sale and usage.PDF p. 50

    India’s First Gigawatt-Scale Data Centre and AI Hub, VisakhapatnamPDF p. 50

    • Announced in October, 2025 with an investment of US$15 billion by a global tech company.PDF p. 50
    • India’s first AI hub with gigawatt-scale compute capacity for AI, cloud, and HPC services.PDF p. 50
    • Supported by Andhra Pradesh government with land, utilities, and connectivity incentives.PDF p. 50

    India’s First Cooperative Multi-Feed CBG Plant – MaharashtraPDF p. 50, 51

    • Inaugurated on October 5, 2025 at Kopargaon, Ahilyanagar district, by the Union Home and Cooperation Minister.PDF p. 50
    • Produces ~12 tonnes of CBG and ~75 tonnes of potash granules daily from sugarcane and molasses waste.PDF p. 51
    • Reduces natural gas and potash imports; promotes circular economyPDF p. 51

    Approval of Proposal to Rename ‘Kerala’ as ‘Keralam’PDF p. 51

    • The Kerala Legislative Assembly passed a resolution on June 24, 2024 to change the name of the state from “Kerala” to “Keralam.” Under the chairmanship of Narendra Modi, the Union Cabinet approved the proposal on 24 February 2026 to change the name of the state “Kerala” to “Keralam.”PDF p. 51

    BCCI Is Not a Public Authority Under RTI ActPDF p. 51

    • The Central Information Commission has held that the Board of Control for Cricket in India is not a “public authority” under the Right to Information Act, 2005.PDF p. 51
    • The CIC held that the BCCI is not covered under the definition of “public authority” under Section 2(h) of the RTI Act (May, 2026).PDF p. 51
    • The Commission observed that the BCCI is registered as a private association under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975.PDF p. 51
    • It has argued that it is not “State” under Article 12 of the Constitution.PDF p. 51

    ‘One Case One Data’ and ‘Su Sahayak’PDF p. 51

    • The Supreme Court of India has taken another step towards technology-enabled justice delivery through two digital initiatives: ‘One Case One Data’ and ‘Su- Sahayak’.PDF p. 51
    • Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant announced the move on May 11, 2026, with the stated purpose of improving judicial data integration, case management and public access to court services.PDF p. 51
    • ‘One Case One Data’ is a digital initiative to streamline case management across different levels of the judiciary.PDF p. 51
    • ‘Su Sahayak’ is an Artificial Intelligence (AI) powered chatbot integrated with the Supreme Court website.PDF p. 51

    Internationalisation of Higher Education in IndiaPDF p. 51

    • NITI Aayog has released a comprehensive report titled “Internationalisation of Higher Education in India: Prospects, Potential, and Policy Recommendations.”PDF p. 51
    • The report identifies internationalisation as a strategic imperative for India’s economic growth, research competitiveness, and global influence.PDF p. 51
    • India inbound–outbound student ratio was 1 : 24 in 2021 and 1 : 19 in 2022.PDF p. 51
    • Indian students’ overseas education expenditure is projected to reach about `6 lakh crore by 2025, which is nearly 2% of India’s GDP and approximately 75% of India’s trade deficit (FY 2024–25).PDF p. 51
    • 8th Poshan Pakhwada 2026PDF p. 51
    • Poshan Pakhwada 2026 is a nationwide campaign of the Ministry of Women and Child Development to strengthen nutrition awareness, early childhood care and development and community participation under Mission Poshan 2.0.PDF p. 51
    • The Ministry of Women and Child Development celebrated the 8th Poshan Pakhwada from 9th to 23rd April 2026.PDF p. 51
    • The national launch took place on 9 April 2026 at Vigyan Bhavan, New Delhi under the leadership of Union Minister Annpurna Devi and Minister of State Savitri Thakur and Secretary Anil Malik.PDF p. 51
    • The theme for 2026 was “Maximizing Brain Development in the First Six Years of Life.”PDF p. 51
    • POSHAN Abhiyan was launched on March 8, 2018 in Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan.PDF p. 51

    NCERT Granted Status of an Institution Deemed to be University (2026)PDF p. 51

    • The Union Government on March 30, 2026 has granted National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) the status of an “Institution Deemed to be University under distinct category”.PDF p. 51
    • The decision aligns with the vision of National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020).PDF p. 51
    • NCERT is now empowered to independently offer degree programmes for undergraduate, postgraduate, doctoral, and specialised courses etc.PDF p. 51

    PM-RAHAT SchemePDF p. 51

    • To reduce fatalities due to road accidents, the scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on February 13, 2026 , and it was officially named “Prime Minister – Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment (PM- RAHAT) Scheme” through a notification issued on February 19, 2026.PDF p. 51
    • As per the statutory provisions provided under Section 162 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, this scheme was notified on 5 May 2025.PDF p. 51
    • Under this scheme, each eligible victim will be provided treatment cover up to `1.5 lakh, which will be applicable for a maximum period of 7 days from the date of the accident, and it will apply to all types of roads.PDF p. 51

    AI-based Bharat VISTAAR’ SchemePDF p. 51, 52

    • Bharat-VISTAAR is a farmer-centric, AI-powered agricultural Digital Public Infrastructure launched on February 17, 2026 in Jaipur by Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, in the presence of Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma.PDF p. 51
    • In Phase-1, this facility will start in Hindi and English and will reach lakhs of farmers in several states including Maharashtra, Bihar, Gujarat.PDF p. 52
    • Bharat-VISTAAR is a single digital gateway for farmers.PDF p. 52

    Motion Against Om Birla and Gyanesh KumarPDF p. 52

    • The Lok Sabha rejected the no-confidence motion against Speaker Om Birla by a voice vote after an extensive debate.PDF p. 52
    • The notices of impeachment motion against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar were refused for admission by the Lok Sabha speaker and Rajya Sabha chairman.PDF p. 52
    • The decision was taken after evaluation by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C. P . Radhakrishnan.PDF p. 52
    • The primary allegation behind this was that the proceedings of the House were not being conducted in accordance with the standards of impartiality and that the opposition was not being given adequate opportunities.PDF p. 52
    • The constitutional provision for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is contained in Article 94.PDF p. 52

    BHASHINI and Voice-First Multilingual AIPDF p. 52

    • The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD) under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) showcased its voice-first multilingual Artificial Intelligence platform at the AI- Led Innovation and Capacity Building Conference held on January 20, 2026 in Lucknow.PDF p. 52
    • The conference was organised by the Centre for e-Governance (CeG), IT and Electronics Department, Government of Uttar Pradesh, and focused on strengthening AI adoption, digital skilling, and innovation capacity at the State level.PDF p. 52
    • About the BHASHINI PlatformPDF p. 52
    • BHASHINI is a national initiative aimed at enabling multilingual, voice-enabled digital public services across India.PDF p. 52
    • BHASHINI expands to ‘BHASHa INterface for India’.PDF p. 52
    • The platform supports more than 36 languages in text and over 22 languages in voice.PDF p. 52
    • It has deployed over 350 AI language models to facilitate translation, speech recognition, and conversational AI services.PDF p. 52

    Uttar Pradesh “Gharauni Act” 2025PDF p. 52

    • The Uttar Pradesh Rural Abadi Records Act (popularly called the “Gharauni Act”) was taken up and passed by the Uttar Pradesh Legislature (assented to by the Governor on January 2, 2026), to provide a clear legal framework for rural residential (“abadi”) property records created under the SVAMITVA programme.PDF p. 52
    • The law is designed to institutionalise rural property cards/records prepared through drone-based surveys under the SVAMITVA Scheme (Ministry of Panchayati Raj).PDF p. 52
    • SVAMITVA status in Uttar PradeshPDF p. 52
    • As per a Lok Sabha annexure (answer dated 29 July 2025), Uttar Pradesh shows:PDF p. 52
    • Targeted villages: 90,573PDF p. 52
    • Drone flying completed: 90,573PDF p. 52
    • Property cards prepared (villages): 68,377PDF p. 52
    • Number of property cards prepared: 10,486,961PDF p. 52
    • As on January 2026, 3.06 crore property cards have been prepared across 1.86 lakh villages under SVAMITVA (all-India).PDF p. 52

    Gyan Bharatam National Manuscript SurveyPDF p. 52

    • The Ministry of Culture launched the Gyan Bharatam National Manuscript Survey on March 16, 2026 under the broader Gyan Bharatam initiative (announced in the Union Budget 2025-26).PDF p. 52
    • It is being described as India’s first comprehensive national map of manuscript repositories to identify, document, and prepare for the preservation and digitisation of manuscript collections across the country.PDF p. 52
    • The survey is a nationwide exercise aimed at identifying manuscript repositories across India and preparing a geo-tagged national inventory of manuscript presence.PDF p. 52
    • The survey seeks to map manuscripts located in private homes, temples, monasteries, libraries, and institutions.PDF p. 52
    • It will help create a national “Manuscript Presence Map” across districts and states.PDF p. 52

    Indian Maritime Doctrine 2025PDF p. 52

    • On December 2, 2025 , the Chief of the Naval Staff released the updated Indian Maritime Doctrine 2025. The Indian Navy Day was celebrated December 4, 2025. The theme for Indian Navy Day 2025 is “Combat Ready, Cohesive, Credible, and Aatmanirbhar Force,” highlighting the Navy’s role in safeguarding the seas for a Viksit, Samriddha Bharat (Developed and Prosperous India).PDF p. 52

    Flag Hoisting at Ram Temple in AyodhyaPDF p. 52

    • On November 25, 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the Dhwajarohan Utsav at Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Mandir, hoisted the Dharma Dhwaja on the Shikhara.PDF p. 52
    • . The flag is right-angled triangular , measuring 10 feet in height and 20 feet in length , featuring powerful symbols like:PDF p. 52
    • Radiant Sun, representing the brilliance and valour of Lord Ram evokes the Suryavansha tradition.PDF p. 52
    • Om, symbolizing the spiritual connection.PDF p. 52
    • Kovidara Tree, an emblem of ancient wisdom and strength. The flag’s saffron color is associated with the Sun dynasty (Suryavansh) and reflects the ideals of Ram Rajya.PDF p. 52

    Chapter 3 · PDF pp. 53-86

    International Affairs

    International affairs is a matching exercise with a reason behind each match. Learn the organisation's members and purpose, then attach a summit's host, theme and outcome. Keep an index's edition year separate from the year it is released.

    1. Bilateral: partner and agreement
    2. Multilateral: members, host, outcome
    3. Reports: publisher, edition, rank

    Build the chapter in eight anchors

    EFTA's four members

    EFTA comprises Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. The source states that Switzerland is outside the European Economic Area.

    PDF p. 53
    TEPA dates and scale

    India-EFTA TEPA was signed on 10 March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025. Its stated aims are US$100 billion in investment and one million direct Indian jobs over 15 years.

    PDF p. 53
    The Swiss visit's 3Ts

    Guy Parmelin's 5-7 October 2026 visit is organised around Trade, Technology and Talent. The source lists migration, young-professional exchange, transport technology, research and innovation arrangements.

    PDF p. 53
    Mobility is not unlimited exchange

    The young-professionals agreement provides for 300 professionals annually from each side, expandable to 500. The migration MoU separately mentions multiple-entry visas valid up to five years.

    PDF p. 53
    BRICS host and theme

    The issue places the 18th BRICS Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 12-13 September 2026. Its theme is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.

    PDF p. 75
    Membership versus participation

    The summit account distinguishes 11 full BRICS members from 10 partner countries. It also counts 32 delegations, including regional and international organisations.

    PDF p. 75
    Payment cooperation

    The BRICS article reports work on local-currency transactions and payment-system interoperability. It explicitly says no common BRICS currency was announced.

    PDF p. 75
    A complete index entry

    The issue's summary lists Human Development Report 2025 - UNDP - India 130 of 193; Global Innovation Index 2025 - WIPO - India 38th. Edition labels must stay attached to the ranks.

    PDF p. 86
    Organisations and agreements are different things
    TermWhat it is in this chapterAnchor fact
    EFTAFour-country trade associationIceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland
    India-EFTA TEPATrade and economic partnership agreementIn force 1 October 2025
    BRICSMultilateral groupingFull members and partner countries are distinct
    PDF p. 53, 75
    Learning aid - not from sourceUse 'M-H-O' for a summit: Members, Host, Outcome. For an index, use 'P-Y-R': Publisher, Year, Rank. These are editorial memory prompts.

    Close the notes. Explain it back.

    Name all four EFTA members, then identify the EEA exception stated here.

    Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. The source identifies Switzerland as not belonging to the EEA; EFTA membership does not automatically mean EEA membership.PDF p. 53

    Explain why 2024 and 2025 both matter for TEPA.

    10 March 2024 is the signing date; 1 October 2025 is entry into force. Signing and legal operation are separate milestones.PDF p. 53

    Reconstruct the TEPA target with a time period.

    US$100 billion in investment and one million direct jobs in India over 15 years. Dropping the 15-year period changes the scale of the claim.PDF p. 53

    Does the summit article announce a common BRICS currency?

    No. It discusses local currencies and interoperability among payment/messaging systems, while explicitly saying no common currency was announced.PDF p. 75

    What three fields should you remember for an index?

    Publisher, edition year and rank (plus denominator where given). Here HDR 2025 is UNDP, 130/193; GII 2025 is WIPO, 38th.PDF p. 86

    Source check. The international rankings table has visibly overlapping rows and awkward publisher/date entries. Its text is retained as source evidence; the guide uses only clearly readable HDR/GII rows and does not certify every rank or publisher as current.PDF p. 86

    India–SwitzerlandPDF p. 53

    • President Guy Parmelin’s State Visit to India Swiss Confederation President Guy Parmelin visited India from October 5–7, 2026 , marking the first anniversary of the India–European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) . On 5 October, he paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat, New Delhi, held bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Hyderabad House , and met President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan . Both countries emphasised cooperation in the 3Ts—Trade, Technology and Talent, alongside developing resilient global supply chains.PDF p. 53
    • India–EFTA Agreement: Established in 1960, EFTA comprises Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. Switzerland is not a member of the European Economic Area (EEA).PDF p. 53
    • India–EFTA TEPA was signed on 10 March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025. It aims to facilitate US$100 billion in investments and one million direct jobs in India over 15 years.PDF p. 53
    • Five Major Agreements and Arrangements: 1. Migration and Mobility Partnership Memorandum of Understanding (MoU): Promotes legal migration and professional mobility, including multiple-entry visas valid for up to five years. 2. Young Professionals Exchange Agreement: Provides for the exchange of 300 professionals annually from each country , expandable to 500, through temporary employment. 3. Transport Technology MoU: Signed between India’s Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and Switzerland’s Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research A. International Relations (EAER) to promote sustainable transport, electric vehicles, ropeways and tunnel technologies. 4. Research Letter of Intent (LoI): Signed between India’s Department of Science and Technology (DST) and the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) to strengthen long-term scientific research. 5. Innovation Implementation Arrangement: Signed between DST and the Zurich University of Applied Sciences (ZHAW) to promote technology transfer, entrepreneurship and the Indo- Swiss Academia–Industry Training (AIT India) programme for early-stage startups.PDF p. 53
    • The inaugural Indo-Swiss Research Flagship Event was held in New Delhi on 6 October 2026, attended by President Parmelin and Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh.PDF p. 53
    • The Indo-Swiss Research Framework (ISRF) aims to strengthen scientific networks, knowledge exchange and academia–industry collaboration. Bilateral scientific cooperation began in 2003, followed by the Indo-Swiss Joint Research Programme in 2005.PDF p. 53
    • The Second India–EFTA Prosperity Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 7 October 2026 , reviewing TEPA implementation and investment opportunities.PDF p. 53
    • India–Switzerland relations are rooted in the Treaty of Friendship signed on 14 August 1948.PDF p. 53

    India-JapanPDF p. 53, 54

    • Shinzo Abe Memorial Corridor Inaugurated in Varanasi On October 7, 2026, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Akie Abe, wife of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, jointly inaugurated the Abe Memorial Corridor at the Rudraksh International Cooperation and Convention Centre in Varanasi.PDF p. 53
    • The corridor commemorates Shinzo Abe’s contribution to India–Japan relations and his association with Varanasi.PDF p. 53
    • It displays photographs and memories of his visits to India and his friendship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.PDF p. 53
    • In December 2015, Abe visited Varanasi with Prime Minister Modi and participated in the Ganga Aarti.PDF p. 54
    • The visit strengthened cultural cooperation between Varanasi and Japan’s ancient city of Kyoto.PDF p. 54
    • Rudraksh Convention Centre : Inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi on 15 July 2021, the centre was constructed with Japanese assistance.PDF p. 54
    • Its concept was discussed during Abe’s 2015 Varanasi visit, making it a symbol of India–Japan cultural cooperation.PDF p. 54
    • Abe served as Japan’s Prime Minister during 2006– 07 and 2012–20.PDF p. 54
    • India honoured him with the Padma Vibhushan in 2021 in the field of Public Affairs.PDF p. 54
    • Uttar Pradesh plans to develop a 500-acre Japan City in the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) region to attract Japanese investment.PDF p. 54
    • Cooperation with Japan’s Yamanashi Prefecture also includes green hydrogen, research and skill development, with a proposed Centre of Excellence involving IIT (BHU), IIT Kanpur and other institutions.PDF p. 54
    • Japan supports major Indian projects, including the Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail, Dedicated Freight Corridor and Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor. 16th India–Japan Annual Summit 2026 Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi visited New Delhi from 1 to 3 July, 2026 for the 16th India–Japan Annual Summit. The main meeting with Narendra Modi was held on 2 July. The visit marked 20 years of annual, alternating leadership visits.PDF p. 54
    • The summit strengthened the Special Strategic and Global Partnership established in 2014, focusing on defence and security, economic partnership and people-to-people exchanges.PDF p. 54
    • It produced 16 official outcomes. The separately announced UNICORN defence co-development initiative was outside this list.PDF p. 54
    • Mineral cooperation focuses on upstream exploration, technical knowledge and collaboration between the Geological Survey of India and the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC).PDF p. 54
    • Japan’s Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) approach broadly aligns with India’s Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) and Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions (MAHASAGAR), supporting sovereignty, international law and a rules-based region.PDF p. 54
    • The fourth 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Meeting is scheduled to be held in Tokyo before the end of 2026.PDF p. 54
    • Cooperation covers JAIMEX 25, satellite-based maritime awareness, naval maintenance in India and defence technology under Make in India.PDF p. 54
    • The Unified Complex Radio Antenna (UNICORN) combines communication antennas into one structure, reducing radar signature and improving naval communication.PDF p. 54
    • AI outcomes included a joint statement and IndiaAI Mission–Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry cooperation with GENIAC.PDF p. 54
    • IIT Bombay, BharatGen and Japan’s National Institute of Informatics will develop large language models with scientific-reasoning capabilities.PDF p. 54
    • SarvamAI and Preferred Networks will cooperate on foundation models and the complete AI technology stack.PDF p. 54
    • The target is to invite 500 highly skilled Indian AI professionals to Japan by 2030.PDF p. 54
    • AI cooperation will be guided by the Hiroshima AI Process and New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact.PDF p. 54
    • Digital cooperation includes the proposed FOIP Digital Corridor and the NIXI–JPNIC agreement on internet registries, IPv6, security, capacity building and exchanges.PDF p. 54
    • Energy cooperation involves Indian national oil companies, Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited, JOGMEC and the Japan Bank for International Cooperation.PDF p. 54
    • The Cooperative Biogas for Growth Initiative supports approximately 1,000 biogas and organic- fertiliser plants through dairy cooperatives.PDF p. 54
    • The leaders supported the proposed clean-ammonia project in Odisha and recognised hydrogen and ammonia as important for decarbonisation and energy security.PDF p. 54
    • The Joint Crediting Mechanism under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement can facilitate bilateral carbon- credit cooperation and low-carbon investment.PDF p. 54
    • Cooperation will continue on the Mumbai– Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project and Japan’s latest E10-series Shinkansen technology.PDF p. 54
    • The Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP) and RIKEN will cooperate in translational research, deep technology, start-ups, healthcare, agriculture and environmental applications.PDF p. 54
    • The National Centre for Biological Sciences–Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and RIKEN will cooperate in biological and neuroscience research, researcher exchanges and joint projects.PDF p. 54
    • The leaders welcomed research exchanges and progress in the ISRO–JAXA Lunar Polar Exploration Mission, or LUPEX, also called Chandrayaan-5.PDF p. 54
    • India and Japan will celebrate 2027 as the Year of Shared Horizons, marking 75 years of diplomatic relations through cultural, academic, youth, business and public-diplomacy events.PDF p. 54
    • Modi accepted an invitation to Japan for the 17th Annual Summit in 2027.PDF p. 54
    • The leaders supported state–prefecture partnerships, including Yamanashi–Uttar Pradesh , and the India–Japan Governors’ Network for Friendship and Exchange.PDF p. 54
    • Yamanashi (a leader in hydrogen technology) partnered with Uttar Pradesh (via UPNEDA) on hydrogen production, storage, and clean energy pilot projects.PDF p. 54

    PM Modi’s State Visit to UzbekistanPDF p. 55

    • Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on 29–30 August, 2026 at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. The two countries upgraded their Strategic Partnership (established in 2011) to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. President Mirziyoyev conferr ed Uzbekistan’s highest state award, the “Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik” Order, on Modi.PDF p. 55
    • Uzbekistan, a double-landlocked Central Asian country, remains strategically important to India because of its location and mineral resources.PDF p. 55
    • Both countries discussed a framework for long-term uranium supplies to India and expanded cooperation in peaceful nuclear energy, geological exploration, mining, mineral processing and value-added products.PDF p. 55
    • Uzbekistan produced approximately 7,000 tonnes of uranium in 2025, with proven reserves estimated at 139,000 tonnes. Cooperation also supports India’s National Critical Mineral Mission.PDF p. 55
    • The countries set a bilateral trade target of US$5 billion by 2030, compared with trade exceeding US$1 billion previously.PDF p. 55
    • Both sides supported multimodal transport corridors and reduced freight costs.PDF p. 55
    • Iran’s Chabahar Port and the International North– South Transport Corridor (INSTC) offer alternative routes to overcome India’s limited overland connectivity with Central Asia.PDF p. 55
    • An agreement between NPCI International Payments Ltd. (NIPL) and Uzbekistan’s National Interbank Processing Centre (NIPC) will enable Indian UPI applications to scan Uzbekistan’s UZQR codes for merchant payments.PDF p. 55
    • Their joint military exercise DUSTLIK (7th edition) was last conducted in Uzbekistan’s Namangan Region in April 2026.PDF p. 55
    • An MoU on Ayurveda and other traditional medicines was signed.PDF p. 55
    • India announced 100 Lal Bahadur Shastri Hindi Scholarships and an ICCR Sanskrit Chair at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.PDF p. 55
    • Both countries signed a Letter of Intent to conserve the ancient Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa near Termez.PDF p. 55
    • India also announced a US$1 million grant for afforestation and ecological rehabilitation in the Aral Sea region.PDF p. 55

    India–Uzbekistan Business Forum 2026PDF p. 55

    • The forum was attended by India’s Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal and Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade, Laziz Kudratov.PDF p. 55
    • Piyush Goyal called for doubling bilateral trade from approximately US$1.5 billion to about US$3 billion within three years.PDF p. 55
    • The forum involved India’s Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, and the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).PDF p. 55
    • Cooperation focused on mining, textiles, pharma- ceuticals, healthcare, agriculture, food processing, information technology, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing.PDF p. 55

    India–SeychellesPDF p. 55

    • Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s State Visit to Seychelles from 27 to 29 June 2026 expanded bilateral cooperation following talks with President Dr Patri ck Herminie.PDF p. 55
    • The visit coincided with the 50 th anniversary of Seychelles’ independence and diplomatic ties with India.PDF p. 55
    • It was Modi’s second visit after March 2015 and advanced the February 2026 Joint Vision for Sustainability, Economic Growth and Security through Enhanced Linkages (SESEL).PDF p. 55
    • SESEL covers defence, healthcare, education, digital transformation, renewable energy, capacity building and food security.PDF p. 55
    • Cooperation also falls within India’s MAHASAGAR Vision—Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.PDF p. 55
    • The 19 outcomes comprised five development- assistance measures, five announcements and nine formal agreements, treaties or MoUs.PDF p. 55
    • India gifted an indigenously built Fast Patrol Vessel, PS Lespwar, to the Seychelles Coast Guard, alongside ten utility vehicles, five sets of Laser Radial-class sailing boats, six ambulances, 500 metric tonnes of rice and 8,500 metric tonnes of cement. Seychelles decided to join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure.PDF p. 55
    • MoUs covered preliminary preparations for a new Seychelles National Hospital and cooperation between HLL Lifecare Limited and Seychelles’ Ministry of Health under India’s Jan Aushadhi framework for affordable, quality medicines and medical products.PDF p. 55
    • NPCI International Payments Limited and the Central Bank of Seychelles signed an MoU to implement India’s Unified Payments Interface.PDF p. 55
    • The Indian Council of Agricultural Research and Seychelles Agriculture Department signed an MoU with a 2026–2031 Work Plan.PDF p. 55
    • Diplomatic training cooperation will facilitate exchanges between India’s Sushma Swaraj Institute of Foreign Service and Seychelles’ Ministry of Foreign Affairs.PDF p. 55

    India–Cyprus Strategic PartnershipPDF p. 55, 56

    • India and Cyprus elevated their relationship to a Strategic Partnership during the State Visit of Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides to India from May 20–23, 2026.PDF p. 55
    • The 2026 visit was the first visit of President Christodoulides to India in his current capacity.PDF p. 55
    • During the visit, he held talks with Prime Minister Modi in New Delhi, met President Droupadi Murmu, paid homage at Rajghat, and participated in a Business Forum in Mumbai.PDF p. 55
    • The two sides also agreed to commemorate the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027 through special events (established diplomatic relations on February 17, 1962).PDF p. 56
    • They welcomed a five-year roadmap for defence cooperation for 2026–2031.PDF p. 56
    • The joint statement noted the MoU between NPCI International Payments Limited and Eurobank Cyprus.PDF p. 56
    • It also welcomed a framework for interoperability of India’s Unified Payments Interface with the Target Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) system of the European Central Bank.PDF p. 56
    • The joint statement noted engagement between the ERATOSTHENES Centre of Excellence and IN- SPACe.PDF p. 56

    Myanmar President’s Visit to IndiaPDF p. 56

    • Myanmar President U Min Aung Hlaing paid an official visit to India from May 30 to June 3, 2026, marking his first foreign trip since assuming office.PDF p. 56
    • The high-profile tour focused on reinforcing bilateral, civilizational, economic, and security ties as part of India's Neighbourhood First and Act East policies.PDF p. 56
    • He offered prayers at the Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya, visited the Mahabodhi Meditation Centre, and paid obeisance at the Sujata Temple to highlight the enduring spiritual ties between the two nations.PDF p. 56
    • The President toured the NTPC Energy Technology Research Alliance (NETRA) complex in Greater Noida to observe India's advanced clean energy and renewable energy research.PDF p. 56
    • NETRA is NTPC Limited’s research and development arm.PDF p. 56
    • Both sides stressed the need to work closely for the completion of the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project and the India–Myanmar– Thailand Trilateral Highway.PDF p. 56
    • Sittwe Port has been developed as part of the Kaladan project and the route connects Sittwe Port with Paletwa through an inland waterway and further with Zorinpui in Mizoram through a road component.PDF p. 56
    • India announced that the number of Mekong Ganga ICCR scholarships for Myanmar students would increase from 36 to 100.PDF p. 56

    India – UAEPDF p. 56, 57

    • Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid an official visit to the United Arab Emirates on May 15, 2026. PM Modi began his five-nation tour from the UAE, followed by visits to the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway and Italy.PDF p. 56
    • During the visit, Prime Minister Modi held detailed discussions with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi.PDF p. 56
    • The major outcome was the MoU on Strategic Collaboration between Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Limited and Abu Dhabi National Oil Company.PDF p. 56
    • The agreement provides for potential ADNOC crude oil storage in India’s strategic petroleum reserves of up to 30 million barrels, including participation in facilities at Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and development of reserve facilities at Chandikhol in Odisha.PDF p. 56
    • It also includes potential storage of crude oil in Fujairah in the UAE as part of India’s strategic petroleum reserve framework.PDF p. 56
    • The primary outcome was a Strategic Collaboration Agreement between Indian Oil Corporation Limited and ADNOC on LPG supplies.PDF p. 56
    • The next outcome was an MoU between Cochin Shipyard Limited and Drydocks World to set up a Ship Repair Cluster at Vadinar, including offshore fabrication, under the Maritime Development Fund Scheme launched by the Government of India.PDF p. 56
    • Vadinar’s location on India’s western coast gives it strategic importance for maritime services.PDF p. 56
    • The other outcome was a tripartite MoU between Cochin Shipyard Limited, Drydocks World Dubai and the Centre of Excellence in Maritime & Shipbuilding.PDF p. 56
    • Another outcome was a term sheet for setting up an 8-exaflop supercomputing cluster in partnership between India’s C-DAC and the UAE’s G42.PDF p. 56
    • The two leaders also welcomed the operationalisation of the Virtual Trade Corridor using MAITRI — Master Application for International Trade and Regulatory Interface.PDF p. 56
    • It is a digital framework connecting customs and port authorities on both sides. UAE President's Visit to India 2026PDF p. 56
    • On January 19, 2026, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan visited India.PDF p. 56
    • A Letter of Intent (LoI) covered UAE participation in Dholera Special Investment Region, Gujarat.PDF p. 56
    • India invited UAE investment in the second NIIF Infrastructure Fund (2026).PDF p. 56
    • Both leaders welcomed DP World and First Abu Dhabi Bank in GIFT City.PDF p. 56
    • Separate LoIs covered IN-SPACe–UAE Space Agency collaboration and a proposed Strategic Defence Partnership Framework.PDF p. 56
    • HPCL and ADNOC Gas signed a 10-year agreement for 0.5 million metric tonnes per annum of LNG from 2028.PDF p. 56
    • Both countries proposed a House of India museum in Abu Dhabi and UAE artefacts for Lothal's National Maritime Heritage Complex.PDF p. 56
    • They reaffirmed the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), launched at the 2023 G20 Summit, and supported the UAE–Senegal- hosted UN Water Conference 2026 for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6.PDF p. 56
